scope: post-measurement storage of finite classical labels in physically noisy memory, separate from source-probe and measurement-work costs

claims.exact_statement: Let X be uniform on [M], encoded into m qubit cells sent through independent amplitude-damping channels A_p with 0 <= p < 1. Let N=sum_i |1><1|_i and let Q=Tr(N rho_bar) be the message-averaged input excitation number, with Q <= mE. For any collective decoder with average error epsilon, d_bin^(2)(1-epsilon || 1/M) <= chi(X:B^m) <= m max_{0<=q<=min(E,1)} F_p(q), where F_p(q)=h_2((1-p)q)-h_2((1+sqrt(1-4p(1-p)q^2))/2). Here h_2 and d_bin^(2) use base-2 logs. This charges cell count, input excitation energy Delta Q, and decoder reliability; it does not bound write work or heat.
assumptions: Independent memoryless qubit amplitude-damping channel with damping probability p over one specified retention interval.
Cell Hamiltonian is Delta |1><1|; Q is averaged over the uniform messages and the stored energy is Delta Q.
Unassisted classical storage code; codewords may be entangled across cells and decoder may be collective.
Uniform M-label source; no side information is supplied to the decoder.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/quantum_physics/thermo_archive/REPORT.md#early-blocker-and-best-scoped-lemma; capacity input is Tang-Zhu-Bai-Wang arXiv:2609.28592v1 Theorem 5.5 and Proposition 5.6; combine its finite-block chi <= sum_i F_p(q_i) with concavity, Jensen, and binary data processing of the correct-decoding event.
claims.novelty_boundary: A model-specific finite-error corollary and reliability accounting for amplitude-damping qubit storage. It does not improve the general OA276 generalized-amplitude-damping archive result, and capacity/Fano composition is standard. The source theorem is a Sep-2026 arXiv v1 preprint and was not independently validated here.

charged: average stored input energy Delta Q

claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the cited finite-block Holevo inequality for an entangled block input, or a code/decoder violating the displayed d_bin^(2) upper bound under the stated channel and average-excitation model.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof audit of the cited finite-block entropy bound, then compare finite-block reliability curves against an explicitly specified generalized-amplitude-damping or device-calibrated memory.

claims.exact_statement: For the same independent amplitude-damping memory and a uniform M-message code with arbitrary m-cell input states rho_x, let Q=(1/M) sum_x Tr(N rho_x) be average total excitation and epsilon average decoding error. For 0<p<1, epsilon >= ((M-1)/M) p^(M Q/(M-1)).
assumptions: Independent amplitude-damping channel with 0<p<1 and ground state |0> fixed by the channel.
Average energy is measured in excitation number over uniform messages; physical energy is Delta Q.
The receiver has a POVM over all output cells and no message-dependent side information.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/quantum_physics/thermo_archive/REPORT.md#early-blocker-and-best-scoped-lemma. For each x, vacuum output probability v_x=Tr(p^N rho_x)>=p^Tr(N rho_x). The vacuum outcome has the same output state for all x; if x_* maximizes v_x, its contribution to average error is >= M^-1 sum_{x != x_*} v_x. Jensen over those M-1 messages and sum_x Tr(N rho_x)=MQ gives the stated lower bound.
claims.novelty_boundary: A direct finite-dimensional amplitude-damping specialization of vacuum/pulse-position reliability reasoning. The M-to-infinity scale Q ~ ln(1/epsilon)/ln(1/p) and sparse pulse-position achievability were already present in prior pure-loss/noisy-archive capital; this is not claimed as a new general result.

not_charged: refresh and lifetime beyond one channel interval

claims.falsifier: A legal code and decoder under the stated model with error below ((M-1)/M) p^(M Q/(M-1)).
claims.next_gate: For a fixed cell-count regime, determine whether a sharper finite-M reliability function is useful beyond this vacuum-event converse and the capacity bound QA-1.

claims.exact_statement: For any integer r>=1 and M>=2, using r banks of M qubits, encode x in [M] by one excitation at position x in each bank. Under independent amplitude damping A_p, decode x if any excitation survives and guess uniformly if all are lost. This has m=rM cells, exactly Q=r input excitations, and average error p^r(1-1/M).
assumptions: Independent amplitude damping on each of the rM qubits.
Occupation-basis preparation and readout are allowed; bank labels and position-to-message map are supplied.
The archive label X is already acquired; the construction is not a measurement protocol.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/quantum_physics/thermo_archive/REPORT.md#early-blocker-and-best-scoped-lemma. There are exactly r excitations; each survives independently with probability 1-p. Any survivor reveals x; all r lost has probability p^r and the uniform-guess conditional error is 1-1/M.
claims.novelty_boundary: Sparse repetition pulse-position coding is standard and overlaps the inherited pure-loss branch. The point here is the explicit cell/energy/reliability accounting for a qubit memory example, not a new coding principle.
claims.falsifier: A violation of the stated error probability under the exact independent-channel model or a hidden resource needed to implement the supplied occupation-basis encoder/decoder beyond the stated cell and excitation counts.
claims.next_gate: Use only as a baseline in a concrete memory-architecture study; do not present it as an advantage until compared with equally informed classical controls under matched energy, cells, error, and timing.

claims.exact_statement: If a physical memory B stores a uniform M-label with decoder error epsilon, then S_2(B) >= chi(X:B) >= d_bin^(2)(1-epsilon || 1/M). For a degenerate memory reset to a fixed pure blank at temperature T, with no side information/correlations available to the resetter, W_reset >= k_B T ln(2) d_bin^(2)(1-epsilon || 1/M).
assumptions: The entire memory register B is reset to a predetermined pure state.
Its Hamiltonian is degenerate during reset and it is coupled to a bath at temperature T.
The resetter receives no side information or correlated systems that can reduce conditional entropy.
The decoded label is uniform on [M] and average error is epsilon.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/quantum_physics/thermo_archive/REPORT.md#thermodynamic-boundary-and-counterexample-to-a-universal-write-cost. Data processing gives d_bin^(2) <= I(X:B) <= S_2(B); degenerate-memory Landauer reset to a pure blank costs at least kBT ln2 S_2(B).
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard Landauer/data-processing consequence under explicit reset assumptions. It prices eventual reset, not measurement write, and can change with nondegenerate Hamiltonians, side information, or correlations.

charged: entropy of the actual archived register
one complete reset to a known pure blank

claims.falsifier: A reset protocol within the stated degenerate-memory, fixed-blank, no-side-information model whose average work is below kBT ln2 S_2(B).
claims.next_gate: Specify a device Hamiltonian and actual reset protocol before translating this conditional work bound into an engineering energy budget.

claims.exact_statement: The measurement-output bit count alone does not fix a universal positive work/heat cost for writing the outcome. In the idealized thermodynamic framework with a pure initialized pointer register, measurement/premeasurement can be implemented as a reversible operation with zero work in principle; the relevant irreversible cost appears when the record is reset or information is otherwise discarded, with work depending on the discarded-information/conditional-entropy and physical memory model.
assumptions: Ideal thermodynamic control model and a pure initialized pointer register.
Measurement outcome is stored reversibly without resetting during the write operation.
No claim about a specific laboratory detector or finite-time implementation.
claims.proof_path: Faist et al. primary paper states the minimum work for logical processes is conditional entropy of discarded information and identifies ideal measurement with a pure register as zero work in principle; Sagawa-Ueda distinguish measurement and erasure costs. See cited works in REPORT.md.
claims.novelty_boundary: Established information-thermodynamics prior art, not a new theorem. It blocks an inference from N18/N32/N62 input-energy costs or archive bit count to an unconditional measurement-work bill.
claims.falsifier: A theorem within the same specified ideal model imposing strictly positive work for every reversible write regardless of initial memory state and discarded information.
claims.next_gate: Avoid scalar write-cost claims; specify an operation channel and its full physical implementation before applying thermodynamic bounds.

global_verdict: No general physical-acquisition thermodynamic theorem follows from the inspected detection and W-Z archive results. The exact physical memory architecture and acquisition/reset interfaces are decisive. QA-1 is a scoped finite-reliability theorem candidate; QA-2/QA-3 give a self-contained amplitude-damping boundary; QA-4 is a standard conditional reset consequence; QA-5 records an established write-cost counterexample.
